title: cron and scheduled work: a trigger is not a transaction

trace.title: Calendar and timezone
trace.detail: cron evaluates calendar schedules and starts commands in its environment. It does not ensure the previous run finished, that the command succeeded, or that a missed business period is repaired. Environment variables, working directory, shell, and timezone can differ from your interactive terminal.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Calendar tick → process environment → command → unique business run → durable work → completion/failure. On restart after a day of downtime, decide whether the app enumerates missing periods or intentionally skips them.

Test overlap, duplicate scheduler instances, failed exit, and late starts. A log saying command started is not proof a report completed.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Two replicas can run the same schedule. A local file lock does not necessarily coordinate separate hosts. DST can make a local scheduled time absent or repeated.
